title: Backend Developer Roadmap
summary: A roadmap for learners who want to build APIs, work with databases, and understand the logic behind production-ready applications.
audience: Best for juniors who enjoy data, problem-solving, and the systems that power apps behind the interface.

sections.title: Backend Foundations
sections.description: Build confidence with JavaScript runtime concepts, server basics, and how the web moves data.

items.title: Understand Node.js and server-side JavaScript basics
items.description: Learn how Node.js works, how modules are organized, and how to reason about request-response flow.
items.whyItMatters: Backend work becomes much easier when you understand the runtime before jumping into frameworks.
items.expectedOutcome: You can explain what a server does and write small scripts or handlers confidently.

miniProjects.title: Request Logger Service
miniProjects.summary: Build a tiny Node-based service that logs request info and returns simple JSON responses.

commonMistakes.title: Assuming server-side JavaScript behaves like browser code
commonMistakes.explanation: The environment, file access, and performance concerns are different on the server.

commonMistakes.title: Copying server setup without understanding the request lifecycle
commonMistakes.explanation: That makes debugging middleware, headers, or routing issues much harder later.

items.title: Learn HTTP basics and REST API design
items.description: Practice routes, methods, status codes, and how to shape consistent API responses.
items.whyItMatters: A junior backend developer needs to think clearly about how clients request and receive data.
items.expectedOutcome: You can build simple CRUD endpoints and explain why your routes and response shapes make sense.

miniProjects.title: Bookmarks API
miniProjects.summary: Create a CRUD API for saving, editing, listing, and deleting useful developer resources.

commonMistakes.title: Returning inconsistent response shapes
commonMistakes.explanation: Inconsistent output makes frontend integration and debugging frustrating.

commonMistakes.title: Ignoring status code meaning
commonMistakes.explanation: Using the same status code for every outcome hides what really happened in the request.

sections.title: Application and Database Skills
sections.description: Move into real backend application structure with routing, validation, persistence, and authentication.

items.title: Organize APIs with Express and clear route structure
items.description: Learn how to separate routes, controllers, validation, and shared utilities so projects stay maintainable.
items.whyItMatters: Even small backend projects become hard to manage when everything lives in one file.
items.expectedOutcome: You can structure a multi-route backend app with readable folders and responsibilities.

miniProjects.title: Internship Application Service
miniProjects.summary: Build a backend for internship applications with routes for submissions, status updates, and filtering.

commonMistakes.title: Keeping the entire backend in one file
commonMistakes.explanation: That works briefly, but it becomes hard to reason about responsibilities as features grow.

commonMistakes.title: Trusting every request payload
commonMistakes.explanation: Backend services need to assume inputs can be incomplete, incorrect, or malicious.

items.title: Model data with PostgreSQL and Prisma
items.description: Learn relational thinking, schema design, and how to query application data in a structured way.
items.whyItMatters: A lot of backend internship work involves understanding data relationships more than writing fancy algorithms.
items.expectedOutcome: You can design simple relational tables and connect them to a Node app using Prisma.

miniProjects.title: Career Roadmap Database
miniProjects.summary: Model users, roadmap progress, and skills with a relational schema and simple CRUD operations.
deliverables: Prisma queries for create and read flows

commonMistakes.title: Treating the database like unstructured JSON storage
commonMistakes.explanation: That hides relationships that are useful for analytics, filtering, and future features.

commonMistakes.title: Designing tables after coding endpoints
commonMistakes.explanation: Better schema thinking early makes application logic clearer and more stable.

sections.title: Reliability and Job-Ready Delivery
sections.description: Practice the backend habits that make your work easier to trust in a real internship setting.

items.title: Add authentication, environment handling, and deployment basics
items.description: Move beyond local-only development by handling auth, secrets, and deployment setup responsibly.
items.whyItMatters: Backend work is often judged by safety and reliability as much as by features.
items.expectedOutcome: You can build a protected backend service and explain how configuration changes between local and deployed environments.

miniProjects.title: Protected Jobs API
miniProjects.summary: Create a backend service with login, protected admin routes, and environment-based configuration.

commonMistakes.title: Hardcoding secrets or database credentials
commonMistakes.explanation: This is a common beginner mistake and a strong signal that deployment practices still need work.

commonMistakes.title: Adding auth without thinking about protected behavior
commonMistakes.explanation: Authentication is not only login screens; it is about deciding what different users can do.

items.title: Debug backend issues and communicate system behavior clearly
items.description: Learn to trace errors, inspect logs, and explain how data moves through the system.
items.whyItMatters: In internships, being able to investigate and explain a problem is often as valuable as writing new code.
items.expectedOutcome: You can debug backend issues methodically and talk through causes, fixes, and tradeoffs.

miniProjects.title: API Debugging Case Study
miniProjects.summary: Document a bug in a backend project, the steps you used to trace it, and the final fix.

commonMistakes.title: Changing code before isolating the problem
commonMistakes.explanation: Random fixes can hide the bug instead of teaching you where the system failed.

commonMistakes.title: Returning vague errors with no debugging clues
commonMistakes.explanation: Good backend systems should help developers learn what went wrong.
